Name: Sandy DeGonia
Badge: Joining a Conversation
What is one insight you gained from completing the Atwoodian Table yourself that might shape how you introduce it to students?:

I would need to make sure to have students summarize small amounts of information. I would also remind them to leave room for them to join the argument. I really enjoyed this activity, and I believe it is quite versatile.

How does the Atwoodian Table idea compare to how you have taught argument and/or responding to multiple texts in the past?:
I have not given a great visual to arguments or responding to arguments. I love the thought of "everyone coming to the table".
What do you notice about the two sets of excerpts in this module (children in fancy restaurants and toddlers and technology)? How do the excerpts work together to invite students to join the conversation? What are some conversations related to topics you teach?:
I noticed that both have different perspectives and a variety of people who should have an opinion on the issues. These excerpts work together by giving several differing opinions. Students are able to form their own opinion based on the information given. I work with students who struggle to express thoughts and feelings. We can use this strategy to learn to problem solve and give better evidence based arguments.
